- **Separate users:** each project runs as its own Linux user. Goonies is 20001, QA Branches Lab is 20002 and QA Child is 20003. This covers Claude's runs, the preview server and git.
- **No admin powers:** sandboxed runs have no `sudo`. A small, strictly checked helper is the only thing allowed to switch to a project's user.
- **Private spaces:** each project gets its own home folder, temp folder, Claude session store, and package-installer caches for npm and pip. Attached files are copied into the project's private space.
- **Preview ports are locked to their owner:** a project can't connect to another project's preview, or take over its port.
- **Prompts are hidden** from other projects' process lists.
- **One loophole closed:** claudebox's original endpoints had no login check, so a sandboxed process could have used them to start Claude outside any sandbox. They now require the internal key and are disabled in sandbox mode.
- **Emergency switch:** a sandbox off setting exists in case something goes wrong. It's been tested, and the default is on.

**Red-team results:** project A tried every attack on project B, and all were blocked:
- listing, reading, writing or deleting B's files
- reading B's sessions, uploads or process memory
- reading the server's keys or token
- stopping B's processes, using `sudo`, or opening up folder permissions
- connecting to B's preview port, or taking it over

A real Claude run told to break into project B got "Permission denied" on every attempt, at a cost of $0.02. Project A's own features all still work: files, git, checkpoints and undo, branches, merge, previews, uploads, live updates and the stop button.

**Your projects:**
- **Data:** everything was backed up first. Your conversations were moved into their sandboxes, and resuming after the move was tested and works.
- **Previews:** Goonies and QA Branches Lab are running again.
- **QA Branches Lab:** it has an unsaved change to `index.html` from before the update. That's your work in progress, and it's untouched.

**What's still not fully isolated:**
- **Visible commands:** projects can see each other's process command lines (the commands being run), but not their contents, settings, keys or prompts.
- **Shared resources:** CPU and memory are shared by all projects.
- **Bubblewrap isn't possible:** the stronger option would require weakening the security of the VPS itself, so it wasn't used.

**Nexus Chat (being built now):**
- **Where:** a slide-up panel on the spider web screen. Press `/` or ⌘J.
- **Access:** it works across every project you can use, and stays sandboxed to exactly those projects.
- **Focusing:** type `#project` or `#project@branch` to point it at specific ones.
- **Spider web:** the strands of each project it touches light up.
- **Undo:** each project it changes gets its own checkpoint, so one "Undo" reverts the run across all of them.
- **Hand-off buttons:** "Send to <project>" buttons for bigger per-project work. You confirm each one, so nothing runs up costs by itself.
- **Cost guards:** a "12 projects in scope" count, plus a warning if you haven't focused it and more than 10 projects are in scope.

  One side effect to know about first: my first test run added a commit to the owner's **qa-branches-lab**: `960e94d "nxeon: edits before run"`. The project already had about 257 lines of uncommitted `index.html` changes, and the pre-run checkpoint committed them. The file contents did not change. I tried `git reset --mixed HEAD~1` to undo the commit, but it was blocked by a permission prompt, so it's still there. The owner can run that command if they want the edits uncommitted again. I fixed the cause: projects that aren't #focused are no longer committed before a run (details under Checkpoints).
  
  **Design**
  - **Shared chat components.** `Chat`, `AssistantMessage`, `PromptBox` and `ContextMeter` now read their store from a React context (`web/src/features/workspace/chatStore.ts`). The project workspace store is the default. Nexus has its own zustand store (`features/nexus/nexusStore.ts`) with the same field names, and it reuses the same reducer and message conversion. The context also carries three hooks: extra content under a run, the empty state, and prompt add-ons (`#` mentions, scope info, cost notice, hidden agent picker).
  - **Scope**, recomputed on every run:
    - Admins get all non-archived projects; members get projects where their effective role is editor or higher.
    - Viewer-only projects are excluded entirely. Access goes through the project's group, which is always read-write, so there is no safe read-only option.
    - Each user gets a Nexus identity uid of 30000+n (`users.nexus_sandbox_id`, never reused). Supplementary groups are the gids of the projects in scope.
    - The run's working dir is a private scratch dir, `/workspace/.nexus/<uid>`. `addDirs` are the main checkouts, plus branch worktrees only when written as `#slug@branch`.
    - No subagents and no preview port. Defaults are Sonnet with thinking "normal" (effort medium).
  - **Project index** in the system prompt is capped at 6000 chars (about 1.5k tokens). Each project gets one line: slug, name, description, tech hint (from package.json or index.html, cached by mtime), branches, last activity and a BUSY flag. When the list is too long it shortens step by step, down to slugs only. #focused projects get a detail block with dir, preview URL and top-level files. The prompt also carries the rules: do small tasks directly, hand off large ones, keep the token budget, touch only listed projects, checkpoints are automatic.
  - **Handoffs:** Claude can end with `<nx-handoff>[…]</nx-handoff>`. It is hidden from the reply like `<nx-suggestions>`, checked against the scope, and capped at 4. It shows as "Send to <project>" buttons and never runs on its own. Sending creates a conversation in that project and runs it in the background. A progress chip links to `/p/<slug>?conv=<id>` (I added `?conv=` support to the workspace page).
  - **Checkpoints:**
    - #focused checkouts get "edits before run".
    - Other checkouts are only checked read-only (`git status`) before the run.
    - After a successful write-mode run, each changed checkout gets "nxeon (nexus): <prompt>", recorded in `nexus_run_commits`.
    - A project that was already dirty and wasn't focused is committed only if the run actually wrote there. That commit is flagged `mixed`; the UI warns about it and asks for confirmation before Undo.
    - Checkouts with an active project run are skipped.
    - claudebox now runs `fixperms` on each project after a Nexus run, so files the run created go back to the project's own uid.
  - **Live web view:** during a run, light flows from the core to each project the run writes to (detected from Write/Edit/Bash paths and the file watchers). Mentioned projects are highlighted while you type, the core animates while a run is active, and the camera re-centres the web above the panel.
  
  **Endpoints**
  - `GET /api/nexus/scope`
  - `GET/POST /api/nexus/conversations`
  - The existing `/api/conversations/:id` endpoints (GET/PATCH/DELETE, messages, prompt with `projects: ['slug' | 'slug@branch']`, compact) work for Nexus conversations. Nexus conversations are private to their creator; anyone else gets 404.
  - `POST /api/runs/:id/undo` reverts every project the run changed; `POST /api/runs/:id/undo-nexus?project=` reverts one.
  - `POST /api/runs/:id/handoffs/:idx` sends a handoff.
  - WebSocket: `run_status` has `projectId:null` and `nexus:true` for Nexus runs and goes only to the owner. New messages: a `nexus` run event (projects written so far), `graph_pulse {source:'nexus'}`, and `nexus_run {commits, handoffs, checkpointed}`.
  
  **Migration v6** (previous version was 5)
  - Rebuilds `conversations` and `runs` so `project_id` can be NULL, with foreign keys off during the rebuild and a foreign-key check afterwards.
  - Adds `conversations.scope`, `runs.nexus_scope`, `users.nexus_sandbox_id`, `messages.handoffs` and the table `nexus_run_commits`.
  - Tested on a copy of the live DB first. Backups are in `data/db/`: `nxeon-pre-nexus-1790971167.db` and `nxeon-pre-nexus-consistent.db`.
  
  **Ops changes**
  - Compose: new volume `data/nexus:/workspace/.nexus`; `up.sh` and the claudebox entrypoint set it up.
  - The `nx-sandbox home` command now also creates `/workspace/.nexus/<uid>` (`1000:<uid> 2770`); the root dir is `0711`.
  - `SPEC.md` has a new §10; `PROTOCOL.md` is updated.
  
  **Verification**
  - Tests: server `npm test` (82, including 14 new in `test/nexus.test.ts` covering permissions/groups, handoff parsing, multi-project checkpoints and undo, index size cap, privacy, compact). Server typecheck passes. claudebox `npm test` (41, including a new Nexus-run test). Web `tsc`, `vite build` and the reducer tests (10, including Nexus touched-projects and `#mention` parsing).
  - Deploys happened only while no runs were active. The owner's previews were restarted after the claudebox restart and are running: goonies-fanpage on 4100, qa-branches-lab on 4101.
  - Sandbox, real run as a member who was editor on one test project and viewer on another, run with `id` and `ls`:
    - uid 30002, groups 30002 and 20006 only (the editor project).
    - The editor project was readable; the second test project, the viewer-only project, goonies-fanpage, `/workspace/projects`, the admin's `/workspace/.nexus/30001` and other homes were all denied.
  - Sandbox, direct helper checks (no cost):
    - Writing to the editor project worked; writing to any other project failed.
    - Uploads were unreadable, sudo was denied, and another user's scratch dir was refused as a working directory.
    - `fixperms` handed files back to the project uid, and the run's files now belong to their project uids.
  - Run costs (all haiku, thinking off): Nexus run with 2 projects changed plus a handoff $0.0217; member sandbox probe $0.0239; handoff run $0.0261. Total $0.0717.
  - Cleanup: the throwaway projects, test conversations, QA member and local dev instance are deleted. The owner's projects, apart from the commit above, are untouched.
  
  **Screenshots** are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-claude/a5a0e1b8-f10f-4557-a424-37ef9c870766/scratchpad/qa/nexus/shots/`: collapsed dock, open/empty, `#` autocomplete, mention chips with web highlight, active run with pulses, finished run with per-project changes and handoff, full height, handoff running and done chips, Undo all, mobile 390px collapsed and sheet. Earlier local iterations are in `shots-local/`.
  
  **Caveats**
  - A "mixed" checkpoint includes edits made before the run, so undoing it reverts those too. The UI asks for confirmation.
  - Detecting which projects a run wrote to is best-effort for the live view only: a Bash write via a relative path might not light up a strand, and its change is only committed to a pre-dirty, unfocused project if the run was detected writing there.
  - Nexus scratch dirs and homes for deleted users stay on disk (ids are never reused).
  - The panel's text-highlight overlay can drift slightly when the prompt textarea shows a scrollbar.
  - Opening a file path from a Nexus message opens that project in a new tab rather than the file itself.
</agent-message>

input.prompt:
You are implementing the token-efficiency plan for "Nxeon Workspace", a deployed self-hosted multi-project Claude Code workspace at /opt/nxeon-workspace. READ FIRST: docs/research/token-efficiency.md (the measured research + ranked plan, esp. section 4 with concrete code), SPEC.md (§8 branches, §9 sandbox, §10 nexus), claudebox/PROTOCOL.md, claudebox/lib/runs.js, server/src/runs.ts (buildSystemPrompt), server/src/settings.ts, server/src/routes/conversations.ts, server/src/agents.ts, web/src/features/workspace/{PromptBox.tsx,store.ts,ContextMeter.tsx}, web/src/features/admin/Settings.tsx. The owner is very cost-sensitive ("be even more protective with wasting tokens") but quality must not drop. Another agent will afterwards add skills/asset library (docs/research/skills-and-assets.md) — do NOT implement skills/library/templates; but DO fix the research's "Phase 0" items that overlap: add "Skill" to EDIT_TOOLS/ASK_TOOLS in claudebox/lib/runs.js and disable conflicting bundled skills (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1 or per-skill overrides — check report).

Implement (each behind admin settings where it affects behaviour, with a single "Lean mode" master switch default ON in Admin → Settings → Efficiency, plus per-item toggles only where useful — keep the UI small):
1. Trimmed base context: env vars + `--disallowedTools` list + `--strict-mcp-config` + `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` exactly as validated in the report (use --disallowedTools, NOT --tools). Ensure `/compact` runs still work (don't pass --disable-slash-commands on compaction runs). Make sure Agent/Task tool stays available where subagents are configured (project runs) and is disallowed for nexus runs (no subagents there) — check current behaviour.
2. Cold-resume protection: track per-conversation last activity and context size; when a user sends a prompt to a conversation idle > 55 min with contextTokens > 30k, the server responds 409 `cold_resume` with an estimate {resumeCostUsd, freshCostUsd} unless the request has `resumeChoice: 'resume'|'fresh'`. 'fresh' = start a NEW Claude session (no --resume) in the SAME conversation, with a free (no model call) summary built from SQLite: last N user prompts, final assistant answers (truncated), files changed (from checkpoints/commits or tool_use events), current todos — capped ~2–3k tokens, injected via --append-system-prompt as "Conversation so far (summary)". Store the new session id. UI: a small inline card above the prompt box: "This chat has been idle 2h — resuming re-reads ~80k tokens (~$0.32). Continue fresh with a summary (~$0.03)? [Continue fresh] [Resume anyway]" with a "remember my choice" checkbox (per user setting). Also apply to nexus conversations.
3. Budget guardrails: per-run `--max-budget-usd` (settings: sonnet $1, opus $2, haiku $0.5; nexus same) — check the flag semantics in the report; `--max-turns` default 30; ensure aborted/failed runs record their cost (estimate from usage events when result is missing, using a price table in settings — make the price table admin-editable with sane defaults for opus/sonnet/haiku 5.x families; get current prices from the claude-api skill/docs knowledge or the report). Show when a run stopped due to budget/turn limit clearly (event error code) with a suggestion chip "Continue" (resumes with "continue").
4. Model-switch warning: if the user changes the model mid-conversation and contextTokens > 20k, show a confirm popover in PromptBox ("Switching model rebuilds ~85k tokens of cache (~$0.34). Start a new chat instead?") with options [New chat with this model] [Switch anyway] [Cancel].
5. Tool output caps: BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=12000, CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=15000 (verify names in the report/CLI).
6. Effort per mode: ask → low; plan/auto/edit → per thinking level as now (off→low, normal→medium, max→high). Remove the useless MAX_THINKING_TOKENS env if the report says it does nothing on 5.x.
7. Prompt frugality rules in buildSystemPrompt per the report's replacement wording (Edit not Write for existing files, no code in replies, README only on create/run-step change, etc.). Keep it SHORT — every token here is paid on every call. Measure the size of the appended prompt before/after.
8. Pre-send cost estimate: in the prompt box footer, a subtle "~$0.02" estimate (based on current contextTokens, model, warm/cold cache state, typical output) — computed client-side from a small endpoint GET /api/conversations/:id/estimate or from data already present. Hover shows breakdown. Keep it unobtrusive.
9. "New chat" nudge: when contextTokens > 60k (configurable), show a gentle hint in the ContextMeter ("Long chat — a new chat for a new topic is cheaper") — no modal.
10. Admin → Usage/Overview: add "tokens saved" insight if cheap to compute (e.g., cold resumes avoided × estimated savings) — optional, only if trivial.

Validation (mandatory, cost-capped ≤ $0.60 total real spend; use model haiku/sonnet with tiny tasks in THROWAWAY projects you create and delete; never run prompts in the owner's projects goonies-fanpage, qa-branches-lab, qa-child):
- Re-measure the per-call fixed overhead with production flags before/after (cheap "reply OK" runs) and report the numbers.
- Smoke-test quality: 5 tiny but real coding tasks (e.g., create a static page with 3 sections; edit an existing file to add a feature; fix a deliberate bug; add a small JS interaction; answer a question in ask mode) with lean mode ON vs OFF on sonnet — compare tokens/cost and verify the outputs are correct (inspect files). If quality drops in any case, adjust (e.g., re-enable a tool) and note it.
- Test cold-resume flow by faking idle time (set conversation last_activity back in the DB for a throwaway conversation) — verify 409 + both choices work and the fresh path produces a sensible summary and a correct answer to a follow-up that depends on earlier context.
- Unit tests for summary builder, estimate calc, budget/turn-limit handling, cold-resume decision, settings defaults.

Ops constraints: back up the DB before deploying (`sudo cp data/db/nxeon.db data/db/nxeon-pre-lean-$(date +%s).db`). The owner is actively using the system. Deploy (`bash /opt/nxeon-workspace/deploy/up.sh app claudebox`) ONLY when no runs are active (`K=$(grep ^CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY= /opt/nxeon-workspace/.env|cut -d= -f2); sudo docker exec nxeon-claudebox sh -c "curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $K' localhost:3000/v2/runs"`); note running previews before a claudebox restart and restart them afterwards (admin: POST /api/projects/:id/preview/start, ?branch= for branches). Test via https with `--resolve workspace.trynxeon.com:443:127.0.0.1`; admin creds in .env (never print secrets). Playwright in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-claude/a5a0e1b8-f10f-4557-a424-37ef9c870766/scratchpad/qa/ (subfolder `lean/`). Use `sudo docker`; respect the sandbox (runs execute via nx-sandbox; don't weaken it). No git commits (coordinator commits). Don't touch Caddy or .env. Quality bar: server `npm test` + `npm run typecheck`, claudebox `npm test`, web `npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npx vite build && node --test src/features/workspace/reducer.test.mjs` all pass. Update docs (PROTOCOL.md, SPEC.md, and a short "Implemented" section in docs/research/token-efficiency.md with measured before/after).

Final report (concise): what was implemented, measured before/after overhead and smoke-test table (tokens, cost, correctness, lean ON vs OFF), total test spend, screenshots of the new UI bits, caveats.

content.text:
Nexus Chat is live. **Reload the spider web page** and press `/` or ⌘J, or click the dock button at the bottom.

**How it works:**
- **Scope:** it covers every project you can edit. Admins get all projects; members get only the projects where they're an editor or owner. Projects someone can only view are left out entirely, because the sandbox can't offer safe read-only access.
- **Its own sandbox:** each user's Nexus Chat runs as its own sandbox user. That user can reach exactly the projects in scope and nothing else. A test member could reach only their one editor project and was blocked from everything else, including your projects and your Nexus scratch space.
- **Focus:** type `#project` or `#project@branch` to point it at specific projects. The mentioned projects light up on the web as you type.
- **Live web:** while it works, light flows from the core to each project it's changing.
- **Per-project results:** after a run you see each changed project (e.g. "goonies-fanpage: 3 files changed"), with **Undo** for each project and **Undo all**.
- **Hand-offs:** for bigger work it offers **"Send to <project>"** buttons. Nothing starts until you click. When you do, it runs in that project's own chat in the background, with a progress chip linking to it.
- **Cost guards:**
  - Sonnet by default.
  - Claude gets a compact project list of about 1.5k tokens, with detail only for focused projects.
  - No sub-agents inside Nexus Chat.
  - A "N projects in scope" count is shown.

Testing used 3 tiny runs ($0.07) in throwaway projects, which have been deleted, and all tests pass. Your previews are running.

**One thing happened in your QA Branches Lab project:** the agent's first test run saved your ~257 lines of unsaved `index.html` changes as a checkpoint called "nxeon: edits before run". **Your file content didn't change at all**, only its git history. Your own next run would have created the same checkpoint anyway. The agent then fixed it so Nexus Chat no longer saves unfocused projects before a run. I've left that checkpoint in place. Undoing it would rewrite the project's history, and that's your call; tell me if you want it reversed.

**Known limits:**
- **Pre-existing edits:** if Nexus Chat changes a project that already had unsaved edits, that project's undo also reverts those earlier edits. It warns you and asks for confirmation first.
- **Missed strands:** a few kinds of file changes made through shell commands might not light up their strand during the run. They're still checkpointed afterwards.
- **File links:** clicking a file name in a Nexus reply opens the project, not that specific file.

**Last step, now in progress: token savings.**
- **Leaner runs:** the overhead sent on every call to Claude will be trimmed from about 17k tokens to about 8k.
- **"Continue fresh" offer:** when you come back to a long chat that has been idle for over an hour, it offers to continue from a free summary instead of re-reading the whole conversation. That's about $0.03 instead of about $0.32.
- **Spending caps:** limits per run, plus accurate costs for stopped or failed runs.
- **Model-switch warning:** a warning before you switch model mid-chat in a long conversation, since that rebuilds the whole cache.
- **Cost estimate:** a small "~$0.02" estimate shown before you send.
- **New-chat nudge:** a hint to start a new chat once a conversation gets long.
- **Admin control:** a **Lean mode** master switch in Admin, on by default.
- **Quality check:** the same 5 real coding tasks will be compared with Lean mode on and off, to confirm results don't get worse. The spend cap for this is $0.60.

After that comes the quality work: asset library, design skills, Unsplash photos, templates and the free quality checks after each run.

  | **Total** | **147,706 / $0.152** | **233,369 / $0.229** | |
  
  I inspected every output file. Lean runs used Edit on existing files and kept replies short. Nothing needed re-enabling.
  
  **What was built:**
  1. **Trimmed base context**: the report's `--disallowedTools` list, `--strict-mcp-config` and `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, plus the trim env vars and the two tool-output caps (12,000 Bash chars, 15,000 file-read tokens).
     - Two deliberate departures from the report: I kept `Skill` available and I don't pass `--disable-slash-commands`. That flag disables *all* skills, which would break the skills work coming next.
     - Bundled skills are off via `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1`, plus per-skill overrides for the three that survive it (design, doctor, plugin-authoring).
     - `/compact` still works.
     - The subagent tool stays available for project runs and is removed for Nexus runs (confirmed in the run's tool list).
     - `Skill` is now in the edit and ask tool lists.
     - Kill switch: `LEAN_MODE=0` on claudebox overrides the admin setting.
  2. **Cold-resume guard**: a prompt to a chat idle over 55 min with more than 30k context gets `409 cold_resume` with both cost estimates.
     - "Fresh" starts a new Claude session in the same chat, seeded with a free summary built from SQLite (first and last 5 turns, files changed, open todos, max 9,000 chars).
     - The inline card above the prompt box has "Continue fresh", "Resume anyway" and "Remember my choice"; the remembered choice can be reset from the context meter.
     - Works for Nexus chats too.
     - Real test with idle time faked in the DB: the fresh path answered a follow-up that depended on earlier context correctly from the summary alone ($0.0072, no tool calls). Resume kept the old session and answered correctly.
  3. **Budget guardrails**: per-run budget cap (sonnet $1, opus $2, haiku $0.5; 0 = no cap) and max turns 30.
     - A run stopped by either limit shows a clear message and a "Continue" chip.
     - Runs that end without a reported cost now get one estimated from their token usage, using a price table admins can edit.
  4. **Model-switch warning**: above 20k context, a popover offers [New chat with X] [Switch anyway] [Cancel] with the rebuild cost.

  8. **New-chat hint**: a dot on the context meter and a hint in its popover above 60k tokens; no modal.
  9. **Admin**: an Efficiency card in Settings with the master switch defaulting on, and "saved ~$x · 30d" under the Cost KPI on Overview.

  - The per-message cost in the chat footer showed the cumulative session cost; it now shows that run's own cost.
  - After a "fresh" restart, the run's cost was computed against the old session's total. Found in the live test, fixed and covered by a test.

  - DB backed up as `data/db/nxeon-pre-lean-1790972886.db` (plus `-wal`) and `nxeon-pre-lean-consistent.db`. The migration added `conversations.last_activity_at` (backfilled) and `runs.cost_estimated`, `resume_choice`, `saved_usd`.

content.text:
Lean mode is live, and I've started the last phase: design and code quality.

**Lean mode results:**
- **Overhead per call to Claude:** Sonnet went from 17,686 to 8,807 tokens (50% less). Haiku went from 22,399 to 11,947 (47% less).
- **Real-task cost:** 5 coding tasks were run on Sonnet with Lean mode on and off. With it on they cost 34% less ($0.15 vs $0.23) and used 37% fewer tokens. Every result was checked by hand and was correct.

| Task | Lean on | Lean off |
|---|---|---|
| Static page, 3 sections | $0.034 | $0.053 |
| Add styled footer | $0.025 | $0.042 |
| Fix bug in calc.js | $0.017 | $0.033 |
| JS toggle | $0.030 | $0.042 |
| Ask question | $0.048 | $0.060 |

**What's now live:**
- **"Continue fresh":** when you come back to a long chat after more than an hour, a small card offers to continue from a free summary instead of re-reading the whole conversation. In testing, the fresh path still correctly answered a question that depended on earlier messages.
- **Spending caps per run:** $1 on Sonnet, $2 on Opus, $0.50 on Haiku, and at most 30 steps. If a run hits a limit you get a clear message and a **Continue** chip. Stopped and failed runs now show their real cost.
- **Model-switch warning** in long chats, with options to start a new chat, switch anyway, or cancel.

content.text:
Everything you asked for is now built, deployed and committed. The final piece, design and code quality, is live, and the before/after comparison is above.

**Quality comparison:** the same 4 prompts on Sonnet, with the quality kit on and off.

| Prompt | Quality kit on | Off |
|---|---|---|
| Coffee-shop landing page | **99** · $0.13 | 82 · $0.06 |
| Photographer portfolio | **76** · $0.14 | 70 · $0.07 |
| Dashboard with chart | **96** · $0.13 | 65 · $0.07 |
| "Make this page look professional" | **99** · $0.09 | 90 · $0.06 |

The scores come from the new automatic checker, out of 100. **On won all 4.** It used real credited photos, distinctive self-hosted fonts, a proper colour palette, and a comparison line on the dashboard chart. Results with the kit off looked generic and had 5 serious issues, against 1 with it on.

**Your decision:** the trade-off is that building a page costs about twice as much, roughly **+$0.06 per page on Sonnet**, mainly because Claude writes fuller, more finished pages. The kit only kicks in for new pages and redesigns, so small edits cost the same as before. I've left it **on**. If you'd rather save the money, there's a **Quality kit** switch in Admin → Settings.

**What's now live:**
- **Asset library on the VPS, 101 MB, all license-checked:**
  - about 12,600 icons from five sets
  - 42 fonts with 32 suggested pairings
  - free-to-use illustrations
  - 560 HyperUI page components
  - 12 style presets, 34 page sections and 6 starter templates (static, Vite, React, Astro, Express, Next.js)
- **8 skills Claude loads when needed,** including web design adapted from Anthropic's own design skill. Together they add only about 800 tokens per call.
- **Unsplash photos:**
  - Claude finds them with `nx-photo`.
  - Searches are cached for 7 days, with quotas per project so the 50-per-hour limit isn't used up.
  - Photographer credit and Unsplash's required download reporting are automatic.
  - Your key never enters a project sandbox.
- **Built-in tools:**
  - a headless browser installed once, so Claude stops reinstalling one
  - screenshots
  - the free quality checker (accessibility, errors, mobile layout, links, outside fonts and scripts)
  - a template starter, and font and icon helpers
- **Free quality check after each run:** problems become a "Fix N issues" chip, and tokens are only spent if you click it. You can switch it off per project.
- **Style picker** when creating a project, with 12 presets, which sets up a brand kit for the project.
- **Design review:** set "Design review" to once or auto in a project's name menu. A critic agent then takes one screenshot and applies up to 10 fixes, for about $0.14 a review. It's off by default.
- **Ask mode is cheaper:** it now reuses the other modes' cache, so its first run writes about 3.7k tokens instead of 10.2k.

**Testing:** it cost $1.22 in throwaway projects, all since deleted. None of your projects were changed. All tests pass, and your Goonies and QA Branches Lab previews are running.

**Two technical notes:**
- The headless browser runs without its own built-in sandbox, but always as the project's restricted user, never as the server.
- Next.js previews switch off one of Next's cross-site protections in development mode, because the preview runs under a sub-path.

**Everything built this round:**
- Sub-branches: sub-projects, git branches, checkpoints and undo, topics, and satellites on the spider web
- Project sandboxes
- Nexus Chat
- Lean mode: 50% less fixed overhead and 34% cheaper on real tasks
- The quality kit

All of it is committed in `/opt/nxeon-workspace`. Reload the workspace to get the latest version.

**Still on your list from before:**
1. Replace the Claude token and Unsplash keys that were pasted in chat.
2. Change your admin password.
3. Lock SSH to key-only login.
4. Reboot the VPS to finish its pending updates.
5. Decide whether to delete or keep the "QA Branches Lab" test project.
6. When you're ready, apply for Unsplash production access, which allows 5,000 searches an hour.
